comments.text_zh: The Ultimate Game Boy Talk[0]（就在页面里列出）是我有史以来最喜欢的演讲之一。如果你把这场演讲发给别人，基本上光靠那个视频，他们大概就能做出一个忠实还原的 Game Boy 克隆。它信息密度极高、通俗易懂，而且非常全面。我会时不时重听一遍，回想它揭示的那些巧妙技巧。对于一个总共只被写过几千个程序的系统来说，能掌握那么多知识，实在令人佩服。[0]: [VIDEO]
comments.text: The Ultimate Game Boy Talk[0] (listed in the page) is one of my favorite talks of all time. If you were to send this talk to someone, with basically just the videe they could likely build a faithful Gameboy clone. It's so dense, easy to understand, and comprehensive. I'll listen to it form time to time and think about all the cool tricks it reveals. Super impressive to have that much knowledge for a system that only had a couple thousand programs ever written for it. [0]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: jchw
comments.why_zh: 受启发开始写 Game Boy 模拟器
comments.quote_zh: 一场精彩的 33c3 演讲 The Ultimate Game Boy Talk，我强烈推荐。
comments.text_zh: 我真的很喜欢 Gameboy 硬件；它有限制，但设计在简洁中显得非常优雅。到目前为止我写过几个玩具级的 Gameboy 模拟器。要让任何东西跑起来都有点挑战，老实说我对音频完全不知道从何下手。尽管如此，还是挺好玩的。LCD 时序是我好奇的一点。似乎直到今天，它周围仍有一点神秘感。我特别受一场精彩的 33c3 演讲 The Ultimate Game Boy Talk 启发，才开始玩 Gameboy 模拟，强烈推荐。[VIDEO]（总有一天我想尝试更多平台的模拟，无论更新的还是更老的，但我觉得要学的东西还有很多，所以还没去折腾。它太开放了，像周期计数这类事情有很多不同的处理方式，好坏程度也各不相同。）
comments.text: I really like the Gameboy hardware; it's limited, but the design feels very elegant in it's simplicity. I've written a couple of toy Gameboy emulators at this point. It's a bit challenging to get anything working, and honestly I have no idea how to approach audio at all. Nevertheless, it's still quite fun. The LCD timings are a point of curiosity for me. It seems there's still a slight bit of mystery around it, still today. I was inspired to play with emulating Gameboy specifically after an excellent 33c3 talk, The Ultimate Game Boy Talk, which I highly recommend. [VIDEO] (Some day I would like to approach emulation for more platforms, both newer and older, but I feel I still have so much time learn about designing emulators that I haven't bothered with that yet. It's so open ended, and handling things like cycle counting has a lot of different approaches of varying desirability.)

comments.author: anyfoo
comments.story_title: Why did I spend 1.5 months creating a Gameboy emulator? (2017)
comments.why_zh: 几乎涵盖 Game Boy 全部硬件，还包括新细节
comments.quote_zh: 这场有趣的 33c3 演讲几乎完整地描述了 Game Boy 硬件
comments.text_zh: Game Boy 模拟器一直很适合做教学或实验项目，因为 Game Boy 平台出奇地简单，所以很快就能看到成果；但它又非常“真实”——Game Boy 取得了巨大的商业成功，有成千上万款软件，所以你有大量软件可以在项目里试用，真正用上那些成果。举个说明 Game Boy 有多简单的例子：它根本没有操作系统，只有一个 256 字节的 boot ROM，唯一用途是显示卡带里的 Nintendo logo，如果校验和不正确就停机（这既是为了卡带完整性，也是出于法律原因）。这场有趣的 33c3 演讲几乎完整地描述了 Game Boy 硬件（实际上还包含一些此前未知的细节）：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Game Boy emulators are always great for educational or experimental projects, because the Game Boy platform is surprisingly simple, which leads to a very quick payoff, and yet very "real" in that the Game Boy was a great commercial success with thousands of software titles available, so you have plenty of software available to try in your project and actually make use of that payoff. One example to illustrate how simple the Game Boy is: There is no operating system at all, only a 256 byte boot ROM whose sole purpose is to display the Nintendo logo from the cartridge and halt if it does not checksum correctly (for both cartridge integrity and legal reasons). This entertaining 33c3 talk manages to describe the Game Boy hardware practically in its entirety (and with some previously unknown details, actually): [VIDEO]

comments.author: ehaskins
comments.why_zh: 为模拟器开发者概述 Game Boy 及其外设
comments.quote_zh: 作为了解 Gameboy 及其内部外设的概览。
comments.text_zh: 我研究 GB 模拟器已经有一段时间了。第一步是理解系统的架构：有哪些不同的硬件组件？它们如何交互？一个简单的模拟器可以归结为：While(true) Emulate_one_cpu_cycle()。每个周期里，你必须产生各种外设的副作用（串行通信、更新显示、生成音频等），处理任何外部变化（按键、串行数据），并模拟下一条 CPU 指令（基本上就是一个大 switch）。我推荐“The Ultimate Gameboy Talk (33c3)”[0]，作为了解 Gameboy 及其内部外设的概览。还有各种测试 ROM 可用，可以验证基本功能。[1][2] 0. [VIDEO] 1. [LINK] 2. [LINK]
comments.text: I've been working on a GB emulator for awhile. Step one is to understand the architecture of the system. What are the different hardware components? How do they interact? A simple emulator boils down to: While(true) Emulate_one_cpu_cycle() For each cycle you have to produce any side effects from the various peripherals (serial comms, update the display, generate audio, etc.), process any external changes (button presses, serial data), and emulate the next CPU instruction (basically a big switch). I recommend "The Ultimate Gameboy Talk (33c3)" [0], for an overview of the Gameboy and it's internal peripherals. There are various test ROMs available that you can use to verify the basic functionality. [1][2] 0. [VIDEO] 1. [LINK] 2. [LINK]

comments.author: TheAceOfHearts
comments.story_title: Nintendo has reportedly suffered a significant legacy console leak
comments.why_zh: 深入 Game Boy 代码前可先了解的背景知识
comments.quote_zh: 在尝试深入任何代码之前，我建议先看看 The Ultimate Game Boy Talk [1]。
comments.text_zh: Modern Vintage Gamer 刚发布了一个视频 [0]，更详细地讨论了这次泄露以及预期中的影响。好奇的人可以在 4chan 的 Pokemon 版块下，回溯所有 Pokemon Prototype General 主题帖来找到下载链接。吸引我注意的泄露之一是 Pokemon Blue 的源代码，一部分是出于怀旧，一部分是好奇老游戏的代码库到底长什么样。首先让我注意到的是这个项目扁平的文件夹结构，里面塞满了数百个文件；我原本以为会更有条理一些。源代码比我预想的更易读、更平易近人，尽管我只翻看了其中一些比较明显的地方和定义。在尝试深入任何代码之前，我建议先看看 The Ultimate Game Boy Talk [1]。[0] [LINK] [1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Modern Vintage Gamer just released a video [0] discussing this leak in greater detail along with its expected implications. Anyone who's curious can find the download links by backtracking through all the Pokemon Prototype General threads under the Pokemon board on 4chan. One of the leaks that caught my attention was the source for Pokemon Blue, partially because of nostalgia and partially out of curiosity to see what an old game's codebase even looks like. The first thing that stood out to me was the project's flat folder structure, full of hundreds of files; I guess I was expecting things to be a bit more structured. The source is more readable and approachable than I expected, although I've only poked around in some of the more obvious places and definitions. I'd recommend watching The Ultimate Game Boy Talk [1] before trying to dive into any code. [0] [LINK] [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text: Personally, I've had more trouble understanding the PPU behavior than i did about the cpu instructions and timings. I'd mostly been going off of The Ultimate Game Boy Talk[0] and the pandocs[1]. In trying to quickly dig up some resources now, I found what at first glance looks like a good blog series[2], so I might take some time to squint at them soon. If any HNer has other good resources describing it, I'd be thrilled. It's been a couple years since I've hacked on my own emulator, and I got through implementing quite a bit of the behavior. As I recall, I was able to get serial output from the test roms, which was pretty cool. I put it down after getting frustrated trying to render the screen. [0] [VIDEO] [1] [LINK] [2] [LINK]
